context:
Goal: batch 81, which holds the Windows time-limit fix you want in before the archive, lands.
Problem (rule): its CI run looks stuck on GitHub's side, and your R26 says no session re-runs a job on its own.
Based on (measured): run 43088666860: the two macOS jobs read "in progress" since 13:48 CST; every step of one reads completed and passed; GitHub's jobs API answers 502 for the other; the run itself reads "queued".
Based on (ruling): R26, no self-made reruns.
Departs from: main, where a stuck run waits until someone acts — the batch runner re-runs those two jobs once.
Meanwhile: the batch runner waits; batches 82 and 83 queue behind 81.
holds: Whether the batch runner may cancel and re-run the two stuck macOS jobs of run 43088666860, once.
home: ruling R26 (no self-made reruns), exception for this run only

options.how: If the two jobs still read in progress at 15:19 CST, the batch runner cancels and re-runs only those two jobs, once.
options.label: Re-run once (Recommended)
options.lose: About one more macOS run of CI minutes.

options.how: Wait for GitHub to finish the two jobs on its own.
options.label: Wait
options.lose: Batch 81, then 82 and 83, wait with no known end.

reply: Overtaken, no answer needed (coordinator 15:27 CST). Both macOS jobs of run 43088666860 had already finished and passed, at 14:18 and 14:23 CST. The "in progress" GitHub showed was stale. What waits now is the run's final roll-up jobs (all-jobs-passed and ci-done), queued since 14:23 CST. The coordinator is checking with the batch runner, and a new question comes only if that roll-up stays stuck.
title: Re-run the two stuck macOS CI jobs of batch 81 once at 15:19 CST?
why: Batch 81 holds the Windows time-limit fix you want in before the archive, and its CI run looks stuck on GitHub's side.
